newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine defence chief tops presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Philippine defence chief tops presidential poll.

text.p: Philippine defence chief Renato de Villa emerged on Wednesday as the business community's favoured candidate for 1998 presidential elections, a survey showed.

The prestigious Makati Business Club said 52.4 percent of its members who participated in the poll picked de Villa when asked who they would like to see as candidate for president in next year's polls.
Senator Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo ranked second at 38.7 percent followed by Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo at 26.6.
Each businessman surveyed was allowed to choose their three favourites to run for president,

Vice-President Joseph Estrada, an ex-movie star with a massive following among the poor and seen by many analysts as possibly the man to beat in 1998, ranked eleventh. He was the choice of 3.2 percent of the businessmen polled.
The MBC, which includes representatives of Filipino and foreign businesses, said 20 percent of its estimated 800 members took part in the survey. Eighty-three percent of those polled were Filipinos.
Subic Bay Metropolitican Authority chairman Richard Gordon, credited with turning the former U.S. naval facility into a bustling freeport area, drew 22.6 percent and ranked fourth.

President Fidel Ramos's six-year term is to end in June next year. The constitution limits a president to only one term and Ramos has said he opposes moves by his supporters to seek constitutional amendments to allow him to run for re-election.

Many businessmen have credited him with turning the Philippines from a debt-riddled economy to one of the most dynamic developing nations in Asia and said they want his successor to continue his economic reform programme.
De Villa, a loyal supporter of Ramos, has not declared himself a candidate but said he is open to the idea.
